bull.b: Contractual and preliminary customer commitments covering more than half of the resized India facility provide meaningful demand validation before construction. If financing closes, this support could improve plant utilization prospects and reduce commercialization risk as Loop moves toward recurring recycled-material sales.

A process that can produce virgin-quality PET and polyester fiber with low operating costs could support competitive economics in recycled materials. This technology positioning may help Loop attract partners, secure project financing, and compete as brands seek scalable circular-material supply.

Secured land, advanced engineering, reliable feedstock sourcing and an experienced joint venture partner indicate that several major development prerequisites are in place. These foundations can shorten execution friction and strengthen the pathway from technology commercialization to operating capacity.

bear.b: The current revenue base remains small relative to the company’s operating cost structure, while negative gross profit and large EBIT losses show that commercialization has not yet produced sustainable profitability. Volatile revenue, including a sharp FY2026 decline, makes earnings power difficult to establish.

Heavy operating and free-cash-flow losses consume capital before the India project becomes operational. With only $1.9 million of available liquidity reported at August 31, continued cash use increases dependence on external financing and leaves limited flexibility to absorb delays or cost increases.

The planned India facility requires substantial equity alongside project debt, while Loop is still arranging further financing and has already used an ATM offering. Additional equity could dilute existing holders, and unresolved funding remains a condition for construction to begin.
